kjv.note: tagged KJV words, not original-language tokens

key: Strong's number: 'H' or 'G' + the number, no leading zeros (H2617, G26)

source.edition: King James (Authorized) Version, 1769 standard text, protocanon, "with Strong's numbers added" -- eBible.org eng-kjv2006, USFM
source.lineage: The tagging is CrossWire's KJV module: OT Strong's from The Bible Foundation (bf.org), NT from CrossWire's KJV2003 project. CrossWire's kjv.conf: "CrossWire Bible Society hereby grants a general public license to use this text for any purpose"; DistributionLicense=GPL.
source.rights_line: eBible.org, the edition's own page and copr.htm: "Public Domain" ... "You may copy the King James Version of the Holy Bible freely." (Crown letters patent: UK printing only.)
source.status: rights ruling for Adam: labelled public domain on the exact edition, see README s.6

not_claimed: The KJV tags are CrossWire's, as eBible.org publishes them; they are not checked here against the Hebrew or Greek, and the rights call on them is Adam's (README s.6).
A KJV tag links an English word to the number of the word it translates; untagged words (italics the translators supplied, most articles) are not listed.
The ot corpus carries no keys of its own: data/ot/ withholds OSHB's CC BY tags. Old Testament occurrences come from the KJV's tagging (corpus kjv), by verse.
Strong's numbering is the key, not a claim that each number is one word: Strong's lumps some homographs and splits some forms (README s.3).

parallels.rule: parallels.jsonl lists a KJV verse only where a parallel Bible does not hold it under the same number; [] = none of its verses does
